name: Agent mailbox between sessions
status_reason: Stages 1-4 live on the Mac and the VPS. Stages 4b, 5 and the CFN side of 6 (fleet workers on the mailbox: role names, coordinator tier, worker outbound queue, mesh rules: main-checkout project names, room mail never wakes, mailbox.sh stats) pass the offline suites; not yet deployed, and live ACL users need ~claim:<owner>:* and ~alias:<owner>:* first.
description: Sessions mail each other across machines and people over one hosted Redis. Readers build inbox keys themselves, quarantine forged to/from and show each msg_id once; sessions can claim stable role names; fleet workers get coordinator mail from their master and queue outgoing mail for the hook; a name already held by another live pane on the host is refused and the session gets its own (claimed name, then status-bar name, then project-id); a watcher wakes idle tmux panes (a new key starts just before its sessions' first heartbeat); room mail is shown at the next prompt and never wakes a pane; mailbox.sh stats flags loops and floods from the log.
purpose: Let any Claude Code session send a request or information to another session, project, room or person, without mail ever counting as permission.
unknowns: Delivery is at least once, shown once: consumer groups and retries can put a message in the stream twice; nothing makes the requested work happen once.
Sessions of one owner share one Redis login, so they are not separate secure identities; a sender can delete its own sent copies.
The hook's taint guard is advisory: it sees only Bash and a list of command patterns.
The coordinator secret is a same-user fence, not a security boundary: any session of the owner's unix user can read the run's secret file.
Sandboxed worker Bash cannot reach Redis, so worker mail waits in MAILBOX_OUTQ until the worker's hook fires; a worker idle with no hook event sends nothing.

sources.claim: receiver_keys builds a contact owner's inbox key only for an address listed in MAILBOX_PUBLIC; otherwise only the owner's own from:<owner> key
emit_msgs quarantines mail whose to does not match the key or whose from owner differs from the key's, drops a msg_id already shown, and still returns every id so it is acked or passed
job_send_later claims claim:<owner>:<msg_id> NX EX 120, XADDs with the stored msg_id, then ZREMs
bounce_entry XADDs the bounce with msg_id b-<hash> before setting the done marker and before XACK/XDEL of the original
the outer hook process trims the spool only after printing the inner process's output, by the ids the inner process rendered

claim takes alias:<owner>:<name> with SET NX, refuses (21) a different holder seen in the last 10 minutes, takes over a quieter one under lock:<owner>:alias-<name>, and keeps the name only if the read-back shows its own session id

emit_msgs labels same-owner mail coordinator only when its coord field equals the reader's MAILBOX_COORD_FILE secret and its from is MAILBOX_COORD_FROM (when set), and deletes coord from every message it prints
flush sends each MAILBOX_OUTQ entry as this session with its queued msg_id, removes it once sent, stops on a Redis or rate-limit failure and sets unsendable entries aside as .failed
the hook flushes a sandboxed worker's outbound queue on every event, outside the Bash sandbox
fleet watch reads <project>-master with its own reader marker, applies host-row worker mail to the roster, prints MAILBOX-DOWN once and falls back to fleet sync while the mailbox does not answer
fleet spawn names the worker <project>-<ws>, creates the run's coordinator secret, claims <project>-master for the spawning session, and gives each pane its own MAILBOX_SESSION

heartbeat refuses (exit 23) a session name whose directory entry is a different tmux pane on the same host, seen within the last 10 minutes (ALIAS_LIVE) and still alive, so two panes cannot share one name

on heartbeat exit 23 for an env-named session the hook writes dup-<session_id>, re-resolves the name with resolve_session (which skips the refused name) and heartbeats again; env-named sessions re-check before every read (heartbeat_before_read)

load_config uses dup-<id> to drop a refused MAILBOX_SESSION for the hook's name-<id> file, else a claimed alias, else name-<id>; each falls back to resolve_session, so CLI mail from a Claude session carries the address replies reach
the hook writes name-<session_id> (atomic rename, only when changed) on every event so mailbox.sh run from that session's Bash uses the same name
nudge_pass starts a newly seen key at the earliest heartbeat of the sessions behind it minus 5 s (NEW_KEY_MARGIN), capped 10 minutes back (NEW_KEY_LOOKBACK), instead of the stream's newest entry
inner sweeps err.* files older than 10 minutes from the cache dir on every run, because a run killed by the timeout never reaches its EXIT trap

resolve_session picks a Claude session's name in order: MAILBOX_SESSION (unless dup-<sid> names it as refused), a claimed role name (alias-<sid>), the status-bar name from the Claude Code sessions registry (registry_name, plus -MAILBOX_HOST_TAG when set), else <project>-<first 6 chars of sid>
